h2: Use the URL extractor for a quick inventory

sections.heading: What this URL extractor returns
sections.text: The tool resolves relative links when you fetch a URL, counts total links, and separates same-host links from other destinations. It does not crawl each result or validate that every link is live.
sections.directAnswer: The tool resolves relative links when you fetch a URL, counts total links, and separates same-host links from other destinations. It does not crawl each result or validate that every link is live.

sections.heading: Use the URL extractor for a quick inventory
sections.text: Fetch a public page when you want to inspect its navigation, resource references, or outbound destinations. Paste HTML instead when you already have a saved response or want to test a snippet without making another request. The TXT export is useful for a simple list; CSV adds an internal or external label for spreadsheet review.
sections.directAnswer: Fetch a public page when you want to inspect its navigation, resource references, or outbound destinations. Paste HTML instead when you already have a saved response or want to test a snippet without making another request. The TXT export is useful for a simple list; CSV adds an internal or external label for spreadsheet review.

sections.heading: How to interpret the totals
sections.text: Internal means the link resolves to the same host as the fetched page. External means it points elsewhere. A repeated navigation link can increase the total, and a listed URL can still be broken or blocked later. Treat the output as discovery data, not a live-link audit. This URL extractor is a first-pass inventory, not a crawler. Use this URL extractor before a crawl when you need to understand the link shape first.

pages.title: llms.txt Generator | Firecraw Tools
pages.description: Generate a starter llms.txt file from a public sitemap, select important URLs, review the list, and copy or download the result.
h2: What does an llms.txt generator produce?
Choose pages with a clear purpose

sections.heading: What does an llms.txt generator produce?
sections.text: llms.txt is a proposed convention for giving AI systems a curated list of useful site pages. It is a plain-text directory that you can review and edit.
sections.directAnswer: llms.txt is a proposed convention for giving AI systems a curated list of useful site pages. It is a plain-text directory that you can review and edit.

sections.heading: Choose pages with a clear purpose
sections.text: Start with documentation, product explanations, pricing context, or other pages that represent the site accurately. A short list is easier to maintain than a sitemap dump, and a human should remove thin, private, duplicate, or outdated URLs before publishing.
sections.directAnswer: Start with documentation, product explanations, pricing context, or other pages that represent the site accurately. A short list is easier to maintain than a sitemap dump, and a human should remove thin, private, duplicate, or outdated URLs before publishing.

The right choice depends on pages, rendering, and how often your workflow runs.","url":"https://firecraw.com/firecrawl-pricing","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Firecraw Tools"},"publisher":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Firecraw Tools"},"dateModified":"2026-09-20"}Commercial investigationFirecrawl pricing: how to think about credits
Firecrawl offers a free tier plus paid usage plans built around credits and volume. The right choice depends on pages, rendering, and how often your workflow runs.
Direct answer: use the current Firecrawl pricing page for exact plan numbers. Credits are the useful planning unit; the number you need changes with pages, features, and refresh frequency.Last reviewed: September 20, 2026. Exact plan details can change, so confirm them on the provider pricing page.
What should you estimate?
Start with URLs per run, runs per month, and whether pages need JavaScript rendering or extraction. A small experiment with representative pages tells you more than a generic plan label.

WorkflowWhat to countLikely question
One-off testingA few URLsIs the free allowance enough to validate output?
Content refreshPages × refreshesWill monthly credits cover the schedule?
Agent or appRequests × usersWhat happens at peak usage and retries?Is Firecrawl free?
A free allowance may be available, but eligibility, limits, and pricing can change. Treat it as a testing path, then check the provider’s live terms before budgeting.
How many Firecrawl pricing credits do I need?
For Firecrawl pricing, measure a sample, multiply by the number of pages and runs, and add room for retries. Separate basic fetches from JavaScript-heavy pages because their costs and latency may differ.
Firecrawl pricing questions to ask before upgrading

- Do the pages require browser rendering?
- Do you need crawl controls or structured extraction?
- Will one API key serve a team or a production application?
- Which limits apply to concurrency, retries, and retention?More guides

What we publish
We build focused utilities for public URL conversion, sitemap discovery, link extraction, and AI-readable site files. We also publish independent explainers about Firecrawl APIs, MCP, Python, pricing, self-hosting, and alternatives.
What we do not claim
This is an independent website and is not affiliated with or operated by Firecrawl. We do not provide the Firecrawl service, promise its availability, or reproduce its official documentation. Product facts can change, so use the linked provider pages for final decisions.
How recommendations work
Some pages include sponsored links. A recommendation appears when the next step naturally involves multiple pages, JavaScript rendering, an API, or structured extraction. The recommendation does not change the price you pay.

[ 04 / 04 ]·FAQ//FAQ//Frequently asked questions Everything you need to know about Firecrawl.BillingIs Firecrawl free? Firecrawl gives you 1,000 free credits every month, which covers about 1,000 pages, and no card is required. When you need more, choose Hobby, Standard, Growth, or Scale. Every paid plan runs on pay-as-you-go: you get the plan's monthly credits, and we add more in 5 USD increments when you run out. You set a monthly limit to cap the spend, or turn pay-as-you-go off. AI agents can get started with https://www.firecrawl.dev/agent-onboarding/SKILL.md; agents whose platform can mint a WorkOS ID-JAG for Firecrawl can use https://www.firecrawl.dev/auth.md for direct authentication.Is there a pay-per-use plan? Yes. Pay-as-you-go is how self-serve billing works. You start with 1,000 free credits every month. On Hobby, Standard, Growth, or Scale you get that plan's monthly credits, and we add more in 5 USD increments when you run out. A 5 USD increment is 1,000 credits on Hobby, 2,000 on Standard, 2,500 on Growth, and 5,000 on Scale. Pay-as-you-go needs a paid plan. You set a monthly limit to cap the spend, and you can buy credits yourself at any time.Do credits roll over to the next month? Credits roll over on Scale and Enterprise. Scale carries unused credits for one month, and Enterprise carries a custom amount. Hobby, Standard and Growth credits do not roll over.Do pay-as-you-go credits expire? Credits you buy stay on your account until you use them. They expire if you cancel your subscription, so use them before you leave.How does pay-as-you-go work? We add credits to your account when your balance runs out, so your requests keep working. It is for paid plans only. Each increment costs 5 USD and charges the card on file. Set your Monthly pay-as-you-go limit in your Billing settings: enter a whole multiple of 5 USD to cap the monthly spend, enter 0 to turn pay-as-you-go off, or enter nothing for no limit. Credits you buy yourself do not count toward that limit.How many credits does a 5 USD pay-as-you-go increment give me? A 5 USD increment gives you 1,000 credits on Hobby, 2,000 on Standard, 2,500 on Growth, and 5,000 on Scale.How many credits does each request cost? Scrape, Crawl, Map, and Monitor each cost 1 credit per page. Search costs 2 credits per 10 results. Interact costs 2 credits per browser minute. The Firecrawl Research Index paper endpoints are free across every category, including AI/ML and life sciences. Agent is in preview with 5 free daily runs and dynamic pricing. Advanced features (JSON format, etc.) cost additional credits. Check out the credits table on the pricing page for more details.Do you charge for failed requests? A scrape that returns no result is not charged. A page that responds with an error status such as 403 or 404 is still returned to you and costs 1 credit. If a charge looks incorrect, reach out to help@firecrawl.com and we'll take a look.What payment methods do you accept? We accept payments through Stripe which accepts most major credit cards, debit cards, and PayPal.Why am I being charged VAT (or any local tax) even though I provided a tax ID? Local tax is applied based on your location and local tax rules, and it's calculated automatically. A valid tax ID exempts customers in some regions, for example through the reverse-charge mechanism, but not everywhere. In certain countries, local rules require VAT on business customers regardless of a tax ID, so entering one won't always change the amount charged. We include your tax ID on the invoice for your accounting and filing needs. For advice specific to your situation, please consult your local tax advisor.

[ 04 / 04 ]·FAQ//FAQ//Frequently  asked questions
Everything you need to know about Firecrawl.BillingIs Firecrawl free? Firecrawl gives you 1,000 free credits every month, which covers about 1,000 pages, and no card is required. When you need more, choose Hobby, Standard, Growth, or Scale. Every paid plan runs on pay-as-you-go: you get the plan's monthly credits, and we add more in 5 USD increments when you run out. You set a monthly limit to cap the spend, or turn pay-as-you-go off. AI agents can get started with https://www.firecrawl.dev/agent-onboarding/SKILL.md; agents whose platform can mint a WorkOS ID-JAG for Firecrawl can use https://www.firecrawl.dev/auth.md for direct authentication.Is there a pay-per-use plan? Yes. Pay-as-you-go is how self-serve billing works. You start with 1,000 free credits every month. On Hobby, Standard, Growth, or Scale you get that plan's monthly credits, and we add more in 5 USD increments when you run out. A 5 USD increment is 1,000 credits on Hobby, 2,000 on Standard, 2,500 on Growth, and 5,000 on Scale. Pay-as-you-go needs a paid plan. You set a monthly limit to cap the spend, and you can buy credits yourself at any time.Do credits roll over to the next month? Credits roll over on Scale and Enterprise. Scale carries unused credits for one month, and Enterprise carries a custom amount. Hobby, Standard and Growth credits do not roll over.Do pay-as-you-go credits expire? Credits you buy stay on your account until you use them. They expire if you cancel your subscription, so use them before you leave.How does pay-as-you-go work? We add credits to your account when your balance runs out, so your requests keep working. It is for paid plans only. Each increment costs 5 USD and charges the card on file. Set your Monthly pay-as-you-go limit in your Billing settings: enter a whole multiple of 5 USD to cap the monthly spend, enter 0 to turn pay-as-you-go off, or enter nothing for no limit. Credits you buy yourself do not count toward that limit.How many credits does a 5 USD pay-as-you-go increment give me? A 5 USD increment gives you 1,000 credits on Hobby, 2,000 on Standard, 2,500 on Growth, and 5,000 on Scale.How many credits does each request cost? Scrape, Crawl, Map, and Monitor each cost 1 credit per page. Search costs 2 credits per 10 results. Interact costs 2 credits per browser minute. The Firecrawl Research Index paper endpoints are free across every category, including AI/ML and life sciences. Agent is in preview with 5 free daily runs and dynamic pricing. Advanced features (JSON format, etc.) cost additional credits. Check out the credits table on the pricing page for more details.Do you charge for failed requests? A scrape that returns no result is not charged. A page that responds with an error status such as 403 or 404 is still returned to you and costs 1 credit. If a charge looks incorrect, reach out to help@firecrawl.com and we'll take a look.What payment methods do you accept? We accept payments through Stripe which accepts most major credit cards, debit cards, and PayPal.Why am I being charged VAT (or any local tax) even though I provided a tax ID? Local tax is applied based on your location and local tax rules, and it's calculated automatically. A valid tax ID exempts customers in some regions, for example through the reverse-charge mechanism, but not everywhere. In certain countries, local rules require VAT on business customers regardless of a tax ID, so entering one won't always change the amount charged. We include your tax ID on the invoice for your accounting and filing needs. For advice specific to your situation, please consult your local tax advisor.

URL to Markdown inputConvertUse example URLClearPublic http(s) pages only · up to 2 MB · no account required
How URL to Markdown works
This URL to Markdown tool fetches a public HTML page, removes common navigation and script noise, and formats headings, paragraphs, lists, code blocks, and quotes. It is designed for a single page at a time.
What you get from the result
The output keeps the source URL, readable headings, body paragraphs, lists, quotes, and code blocks together in one copyable document. Use it to review an article, prepare context for a prompt, or create a starting point for documentation without manually selecting the page text. This URL to Markdown workflow keeps the first result easy to inspect.
What it cannot do
Pages that require sign-in, heavy JavaScript rendering, anti-bot challenges, or more than 2 MB may fail or produce incomplete content. Do not submit private URLs. A successful response is still a best-effort conversion, so review important facts before publishing or automating the result.
Need a larger crawl?

What URLs can the converter process?It accepts public HTTP and HTTPS pages and rejects private network targets, authenticated URLs, and responses over the tool size limit.
Why is my page incomplete?Login walls, JavaScript-only content, anti-bot challenges, and unsupported markup can limit a single-page conversion.

sections.heading: What this URL extractor returns
sections.text: The tool resolves relative links when you fetch a URL, counts total links, and separates same-host links from other destinations. It does not crawl each result or validate that every link is live.
sections.directAnswer: The tool resolves relative links when you fetch a URL, counts total links, and separates same-host links from other destinations. It does not crawl each result or validate that every link is live.

sections.heading: Use the URL extractor for a quick inventory
sections.text: Fetch a public page when you want to inspect its navigation, resource references, or outbound destinations. Paste HTML instead when you already have a saved response or want to test a snippet without making another request. The TXT export is useful for a simple list; CSV adds an internal or external label for spreadsheet review.
sections.directAnswer: Fetch a public page when you want to inspect its navigation, resource references, or outbound destinations. Paste HTML instead when you already have a saved response or want to test a snippet without making another request. The TXT export is useful for a simple list; CSV adds an internal or external label for spreadsheet review.

sections.heading: How to interpret the totals
sections.text: Internal means the link resolves to the same host as the fetched page. External means it points elsewhere. A repeated navigation link can increase the total, and a listed URL can still be broken or blocked later. Treat the output as discovery data, not a live-link audit. This URL extractor is a first-pass inventory, not a crawler. Use this URL extractor before a crawl when you need to understand the link shape first.

This independent guide maps the pieces so you can choose the right path.","url":"https://firecraw.com/firecrawl","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Firecraw Tools"},"publisher":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Firecraw Tools"},"dateModified":"2026-09-20"}Independent product guideWhat is Firecrawl?
Firecrawl is a web data service for fetching, crawling, and extracting website content for developer and AI workflows. This independent guide maps the pieces so you can choose the right path.
What does Firecrawl do?
The service turns public web pages into structured or Markdown-friendly data through managed endpoints. A single scrape is useful for one page; a crawl follows links across a site; extraction adds a schema when a predictable shape matters.
Where does Firecrawl fit?
Scrape
Fetch one URL and return readable content, HTML, or metadata.
Crawl
Discover and process multiple pages when one URL is not enough.
Agent access
Use API or MCP patterns to let an AI workflow request web context.
Choose by workload

NeedStart withWhy
One known public pageScrapeLowest-complexity path for readable content or metadata.
Many related pagesCrawlDiscovery and repeat retrieval matter more than a one-off fetch.
Structured recordsExtractionA schema makes downstream validation easier.
Agent-controlled retrievalAPI or MCPUse a tool interface when an application or agent needs web context on demand.Before committing, test representative pages with the output format your application actually stores. Check JavaScript-heavy pages, failure behavior, latency, usage limits, and how much operational work your team wants to own.
What this overview cannot decide for you
A feature list cannot predict the result on every site. Your pages may have different scripts, access rules, languages, or data shapes than a provider demo. Use a small, representative sample and record completeness, response time, retries, and cleanup needs. Keep the sample and acceptance criteria so a later plan change can be compared against the same baseline.

[ 04 / 04 ]·FAQ//FAQ//Frequently asked questions Everything you need to know about Firecrawl.BillingIs Firecrawl free? Firecrawl gives you 1,000 free credits every month, which covers about 1,000 pages, and no card is required. When you need more, choose Hobby, Standard, Growth, or Scale. Every paid plan runs on pay-as-you-go: you get the plan's monthly credits, and we add more in 5 USD increments when you run out. You set a monthly limit to cap the spend, or turn pay-as-you-go off. AI agents can get started with https://www.firecrawl.dev/agent-onboarding/SKILL.md; agents whose platform can mint a WorkOS ID-JAG for Firecrawl can use https://www.firecrawl.dev/auth.md for direct authentication.Is there a pay-per-use plan? Yes. Pay-as-you-go is how self-serve billing works. You start with 1,000 free credits every month. On Hobby, Standard, Growth, or Scale you get that plan's monthly credits, and we add more in 5 USD increments when you run out. A 5 USD increment is 1,000 credits on Hobby, 2,000 on Standard, 2,500 on Growth, and 5,000 on Scale. Pay-as-you-go needs a paid plan. You set a monthly limit to cap the spend, and you can buy credits yourself at any time.Do credits roll over to the next month? Credits roll over on Scale and Enterprise. Scale carries unused credits for one month, and Enterprise carries a custom amount. Hobby, Standard and Growth credits do not roll over.Do pay-as-you-go credits expire? Credits you buy stay on your account until you use them. They expire if you cancel your subscription, so use them before you leave.How does pay-as-you-go work? We add credits to your account when your balance runs out, so your requests keep working. It is for paid plans only. Each increment costs 5 USD and charges the card on file. Set your Monthly pay-as-you-go limit in your Billing settings: enter a whole multiple of 5 USD to cap the monthly spend, enter 0 to turn pay-as-you-go off, or enter nothing for no limit. Credits you buy yourself do not count toward that limit.How many credits does a 5 USD pay-as-you-go increment give me? A 5 USD increment gives you 1,000 credits on Hobby, 2,000 on Standard, 2,500 on Growth, and 5,000 on Scale.How many credits does each request cost? Scrape, Crawl, Map, and Monitor each cost 1 credit per page. Search costs 2 credits per 10 results. Interact costs 2 credits per browser minute. The Firecrawl Research Index paper endpoints are free across every category, including AI/ML and life sciences. Agent is in preview with 5 free daily runs and dynamic pricing. Advanced features (JSON format, etc.) cost additional credits. Check out the credits table on the pricing page for more details.Do you charge for failed requests? A scrape that returns no result is not charged. A page that responds with an error status such as 403 or 404 is still returned to you and costs 1 credit. If a charge looks incorrect, reach out to help@firecrawl.com and we'll take a look.What payment methods do you accept? We accept payments through Stripe which accepts most major credit cards, debit cards, and PayPal.Why am I being charged VAT (or any local tax) even though I provided a tax ID? Local tax is applied based on your location and local tax rules, and it's calculated automatically. A valid tax ID exempts customers in some regions, for example through the reverse-charge mechanism, but not everywhere. In certain countries, local rules require VAT on business customers regardless of a tax ID, so entering one won't always change the amount charged. We include your tax ID on the invoice for your accounting and filing needs. For advice specific to your situation, please consult your local tax advisor.

A 5 USD increment is 1,000 credits on Hobby, 2,000 on Standard, 2,500 on Growth, and 5,000 on Scale. Pay-as-you-go needs a paid plan. You set a monthly limit to cap the spend, and you can buy credits yourself at any time.Do credits roll over to the next month? Credits roll over on Scale and Enterprise. Scale carries unused credits for one month, and Enterprise carries a custom amount. Hobby, Standard and Growth credits do not roll over.Do pay-as-you-go credits expire? Credits you buy stay on your account until you use them. They expire if you cancel your subscription, so use them before you leave.How does pay-as-you-go work? We add credits to your account when your balance runs out, so your requests keep working. It is for paid plans only. Each increment costs 5 USD and charges the card on file. Set your Monthly pay-as-you-go limit in your Billing settings: enter a whole multiple of 5 USD to cap the monthly spend, enter 0 to turn pay-as-you-go off, or enter nothing for no limit. Credits you buy yourself do not count toward that limit.How many credits does a 5 USD pay-as-you-go increment give me? A 5 USD increment gives you 1,000 credits on Hobby, 2,000 on Standard, 2,500 on Growth, and 5,000 on Scale.How many credits does each request cost? Scrape, Crawl, Map, and Monitor each cost 1 credit per page. Search costs 2 credits per 10 results. Interact costs 2 credits per browser minute. The Firecrawl Research Index paper endpoints are free across every category, including AI/ML and life sciences. Agent is in preview with 5 free daily runs and dynamic pricing. Advanced features (JSON format, etc.) cost additional credits. Check out the credits table on the pricing page for more details.Do you charge for failed requests? A scrape that returns no result is not charged. A page that responds with an error status such as 403 or 404 is still returned to you and costs 1 credit. If a charge looks incorrect, reach out to help@firecrawl.com and we'll take a look.What payment methods do you accept? We accept payments through Stripe which accepts most major credit cards, debit cards, and PayPal.Why am I being charged VAT (or any local tax) even though I provided a tax ID? Local tax is applied based on your location and local tax rules, and it's calculated automatically. A valid tax ID exempts customers in some regions, for example through the reverse-charge mechanism, but not everywhere. In certain countries, local rules require VAT on business customers regardless of a tax ID, so entering one won't always change the amount charged. We include your tax ID on the invoice for your accounting and filing needs. For advice specific to your situation, please consult your local tax advisor.
